one_line: A to-camera parenting-expert video with burned-in captions and acted-out lines, holding a swaddled bundle, showing three things parents say that blame the new baby and how to reword them (the 'Don't Blame the Baby' hack).

hook.visual: Woman in a black sweater and a patterned headband speaking straight to camera in a bright room (wooden dresser, lamp, plant, framed print). One serif caption box at the lower third. No b-roll, cut or motion graphic in the first 6s.
hook.on_screen_text: "Here is a life changing hack to prevent sibling rivalry and jealousy." (0-6s), then "Don't Blame the Baby" (6s) (English on screen)
hook.first_spoken_line: Here's a life-changing hack to prevent sibling rivalry and jealousy, it's called don't blame the baby (English, Whisper)
hook.why_it_stops_the_scroll: Observed: states the outcome (prevent sibling rivalry and jealousy) and names the technique within 6.8s. Inferred: 'Don't Blame the Baby' is a short, quotable rule, and parents with a new or expected second child self-select immediately.

beats.observed: Direct-to-camera, same caption box held for 6s; at about 6s both hands sweep outward as she says the technique name.
beats.spoken: Here's a life-changing hack to prevent sibling rivalry and jealousy, it's called don't blame the baby.
beats.on_screen_text: Here is a life changing hack to prevent sibling rivalry and jealousy. / Don't Blame the Baby

beats.observed: Caption poses a shared-guilt question; she leans in.
beats.spoken: How often have we all said things like...
beats.on_screen_text: How often have we all said things like...

beats.observed: She cradles a swaddled bundle in a teal snowflake-print blanket and recites the lines in character, turning and gesturing. A black pill label with a red X sits at the top the whole time. Whether the bundle is a doll or a baby is not visible.
beats.spoken: No, I can't play with you right now. I'm feeding the baby. Charlie, be quiet. The baby is sleeping. No, we are not going to the playground right now. Your sister is too fussy.
beats.on_screen_text: Label: "❌BLAMES THE BABY". Quotes: "No, I can't play with you right now. I'm feeding the baby." / "Charlie, be quiet. The baby is sleeping." / "No, we are not going to the playground right now. Your sister is too fussy."

beats.observed: She puts the bundle down and speaks to camera with open hands. From about 30s a black box at the top reads the effect of the behaviour.
beats.spoken: Now think about this from your toddler's perspective. Ever since this little tiny thing that's crying all the time came into their lives, all of a sudden they can't be loud, mommy doesn't play with me as much anymore and I can't go to the park, all of a sudden life is not very fun, and you want to know why?
beats.on_screen_text: Now think about this from your toddler's perspective... / Ever since this little, tiny thing that's crying all the time came into their lives... / ...all of a sudden, they can't be loud, mommy doesn't play with me as much anymore, and I can't go to the park. / Top box: "This can lead to jealousy and sibling rivalry." / All of a sudden, life is not very fun and you want to know why?

beats.observed: Raised index finger at 38s, pointing gesture at 40s. A white hand-drawn swoosh underline appears under the caption at about 44s.
beats.spoken: It's because of my baby brother or sister. Instead say the exact same things. You can still say no, just don't blame the baby.
beats.on_screen_text: It's because of my baby brother or sister. / Instead, say the exact same things. You can still say no. / Just don't blame the baby.

beats.observed: She picks the swaddled bundle up again. The top label flips to a green check pill. She looks down at the bundle while saying the line.
beats.spoken: Yes, I would love to play with you. I need six minutes and then I will play with you.
beats.on_screen_text: Label: "✅DOESN'T BLAME THE BABY". Quote: "Yes! I would love to play with you. I need six minutes, and then I will play with you."

beats.observed: Same framing and green label. The last sampled frame at 56s is mid-sentence; no outro card or logo appears in any frame.
beats.spoken: We can't go to the park right now, but we can go to the park after nap time today. Okay?
beats.on_screen_text: "We can't go to the park right now, but we CAN go to the park after nap time today. Okay?"

payoff: The rule is named at about 6s. The concrete reworded scripts arrive at 46-57s, the last 12 seconds. Only two of the three 'wrong' lines get a rewrite: the 'be quiet, the baby is sleeping' line does not.
cta: None inside the video (nothing in the frames or transcript). The caption points to the account's course, Winning the Toddler Stage (ages 1-6), link in bio.
share_or_comment_trigger: Inferred: parents recognise their own sentences in the first 19s and send it to a partner or a friend expecting a second child; the two scripts are copyable. Comments are 889 on 3.51M views (about 0.03%), low against 84.5K likes. Saves and shares are not in meta.json.
why_it_worked: 3.51M views, 11.9x the account median of 295K, with a 2.4% like rate. Strong organic-looking reach for a 58s selfie video with no b-roll.

Wrong-then-right structure is visible, not just claimed: the label flips from a red X 'BLAMES THE BABY' (10-18s) to a green check 'DOESN'T BLAME THE BABY' (46-56s) while the same situations are reworded (observed).
A toddler's-voice monologue at 20-36s gives the emotional reason, turning advice into empathy and making the rule memorable (inferred).
paid_signal: no: like_rate_pct is 2.4, well above the 0.3 threshold, and there are no ad cues in the frames.

solo_route.how: 1) Barter with a child psychologist or early-years educator for three 'say this instead' pairs for the new-sibling transition, and have them check your wording. 2) Film the expert in one take, or build the video as text cards over a plain background using the expert's voice note. 3) In CapCut or Canva add the red X pill over the 'wrong' lines and the green check pill over the 'right' lines, and keep the wrong and right lines about the same situation. 4) Use a blanket-wrapped doll or pillow as the prop instead of a baby. 5) End with a LumeBook card: a personalised book where the older sibling is the hero, offered as a big-sibling gift idea.
solo_route.needs: A credentialed barter expert and their sign-off. No child or baby is needed on camera. Do not present parenting advice yourself, since the credibility comes from the expert.

lumebook_version.concept: Expert-led swap video for the new-sibling transition using the same red X and green check pills. Close on the gifter angle: a personalised LumeBook where the older child is the hero, shown as one idea for the big sibling next to the expert's scripts.

evidence_notes: Transcript is clean English and agrees with the captions (Charlie, six minutes, park after nap time), so reliability is high. Whisper's timing runs about 1-2s ahead of the caption changes. The caption on the post says 'I need 5 minutes', lists three steps (connect first, tell her what to expect, put her in charge) and a 10-minutes-a-day tip; the video says six minutes and does not include the 'put her in charge' step. The swaddled bundle is observed only as a bundle in a teal snowflake-print blanket; I cannot tell if it is a doll or a baby. I did not identify the presenter; made_by 'expert_self' is inferred from the account name 'Toddler & Big Kid Experts'. The video ends at 57.8s on the last line with no outro in frames or transcript, so a loop is possible but cannot be verified. Duration from frames/index.json.
